newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end sharply higher helped by weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end sharply higher helped by weak yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended Tuesday's session with sharp gains after export-strong shares rallied, inspired by the yen's weakness against the dollar, brokers said. But they said sectors burdened by bad loans were still weak.
The 225-share Nikkei average rose 306.03 points or 1.73 percent to end at 18,021.70. Its June futures were 390 points higher at 18,040.

"A small handful of shares supported by a weakening yen boosted the indices, but securities, construction and most banks were still pitifully weak and declining issues outnumbered the gainers," said Akihiro Naemura, Okasan Securities general manager.
Losing issues outnumbered gainers 646 shares to 497, while 99 issues were unchanged. Turnover was some 477 million shares, up from 410 million on Monday.
The yen's fall to 125.87 yen to the dollar in early morning trade in Tokyo powered a rally in car issues and electricals.

Comments by government officials, particularly from cabinet minister Kabun Muto, who was quoted as urging the Bank of Japan to consider the possibility of raising the official discount rate, briefly supported the yen.
But in the afternoon the yen slumped to 126 yen to the dollar, its lowest level since January 1993.
"A weak yen will improve earnings of blue-chip issues to some extent," said Kiyoshi Kimura, head of research at Societe Generale Securities Ltd.

"Japanese high-tech issues are disregarding the weakening of their U.S. counterparts, which is unnatural," Kimura added. "The buyers, namely public funds, are buying the shares because there is nothing else worth investing in at the moment."
Sony Corp jumped 140 yen to 9,120. Canon Inc added 110 yen to 2,930. NEC Corp leapt 40 yen to 1,520.
Carmakers were driven higher by the faltering yen. Toyota Motor Corp climbed 180 yen to 3,460 and its group firm Denso Corp rose 210 yen to 2,590. Honda Motor Co Ltd added 30 yen to 3,880.

Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), which has been falling steadily since March 25, ended with slight gains due to buy-backs, brokers said. It added nine yen to end at 170. Trade totalled 11.311 million shares, making it the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

"NCB has fallen pretty heavily in past sessions and it was about time that buy-backs appeared," a trader at a foreign brokerage said. "But apart from that, there is nothing else encouraging about the shares."
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd also rebounded to finish with a 10 yen gain at 1,900, after falling to 1,810.

Brokerages and builders were battered by more dissolution of cross-shareholdings. Scandal-tainted Nomura Securities Co Ltd ended down 20 yen at 1,240 and Nikko Securities Co Ltd finished 15 yen lower at 601.
General contractor Kajima Corp shed 34 yen to 495 while Shimizu Corp slipped 26 yen to 562.
Brokers said portfolio reshuffling and the elimination of cross-shareholdings would probably continue for most of April.
After selling off unwanted issues, some investors were beginning to turn to raw materials such as steel and chemicals, brokers said.
Nippon Steel Corp rose four yen to 363 and Nippon Chemical Industrial Co Ltd jumped 43 yen to 683.

Warehouses, precision instruments, credit/lease, pharmaceuticals and automobiles were at the top of the list of gaining sectors. Securities, air transport, banks, construction and transport equipment led the decliners.

The TOPIX index rose a moderate 10.22 points or 0.75 percent to 1,365.05. The Nikkei 300 added 2.83 points or 1.08 percent to 265.07. The second section index, however, slid 19.74 points or 1.23 percent to 1,582.87. Turnover was 7.78 million shares, compared with 8.19 million on Monday.
The over-the-counter index was down 14.54 points or 1.32 percent at 1,088.00 in late Tokyo afternoon trade.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
